description: The Kroger Co. is one of the largest U.S. grocery retailers, operating supermarkets under banners including Kroger, Ralphs, Fred Meyer, King Soopers, Fry’s, Smith’s, Harris Teeter, Mariano’s, and others. In addition to grocery stores, its network includes fuel centers, pharmacies, and digital shopping services. Customers can order groceries online for same-day Kroger Pickup—formerly ClickList—or delivery. Kroger has expanded its offerings for professional and at-home meal occasions through prepared foods and its Home Chef business, while growing its private-label portfolio with Kroger Mercado, a Hispanic-inspired line launched in 2023 with more than 50 products.

title: Kroger

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription:
The highlight of 2022 for Kroger—already the country's largest grocery store chain—was the October announcement of a $24.6 billion merger with competitor Safeway-Albertsons. Kroger CEO Rodney McMullen vowed to take legal action if regulators blocked the deal over concerns of corporate consolidation. Approval of the deal is not expected until early 2024.

  • Kroger’s delivery business grew 22% in 2022, largely driven by the national rollout of its paid subscription program Kroger Boost, which offers free delivery on orders over $35 and hopes to compete with the likes of Amazon Fresh and Instacart.

  • After questions surrounding compensation for employees, Kroger responded by investing $800 million into raises for frontline employees in 2022, raising minimum pay for all its employees to $18 an hour.

  • In the fourth quarter of 2022 Kroger ended its relationship with the Cigna-owned pharmacy benefit manager Express Scripts after contract renewal talks broke down. The rupture was expected to cost Kroger $100 million in sales at its in-store pharmacies.

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription: During a time of high inflation and supply-chain issues, grocery chain Kroger remained competitive by focusing on its digital infrastructure; the company reported in 2021 that its e-commerce sales had grown by 113% over the previous two years. Investors benefited from the continued pandemic boom in grocery sales, with Kroger shareholders earning a total return of 45% in 2021. Some Kroger workers, however, felt left out: In a survey of more than 36,000 Kroger employees, published by the Economic Roundtable in January 2022, about three-quarters reported suffering from food insecurity. (Kroger has characterized the survey as misleading and says that it pays wages and benefits higher than those of its retail peers.)

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: Before the pandemic, Kroger had been trying to become a bigger e-commerce player, with some success in the grocery wars with Walmart and Amazon. But the COVID-19 outbreak forced the grocer’s hand and led it to speed up a number of digital initiatives to support faster delivery. The upshot is that Kroger’s digital business doubled in 2020, leading to an 8.4% increase in overall sales. The company is now eyeing a target $20 billion in annual online sales by 2023. To do so, it has opened a 375,000-square-foot, fully automated distribution center outside Cincinnati, with nine other facilities coming on line in the next two years.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: Kroger has performed consistently amid stiff competition from the likes of Walmart, which already has an outsize share of U.S. grocery sales, and Amazon, which is making increasing inroads into the segment. Kroger's same-store sales edged ahead 2% in 2019, which is about average for U.S. grocers, while operating profits increased 7.5%. After a slow start in ecommerce, the Cincinnati-based company has been investing to ramp up its online operations through a partnership with U.K. grocer Ocado. It aims to eventually have 20 highly automated fulfilment centers operating across the U.S. The first three of these warehouses—in Ohio, Georgia and Florida—are due to open in 2021. At least one prominent investor likes Kroger’s prospects: Warren Buffett’s Berkshire Hathaway revealed it had taken a 2.4% stake in the grocer in the fourth quarter.
